A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same operator-based stochastic-interpolant framework. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-generation and inpainting results, phi4 posterior-sampling experiments, and maze-planning outcomes in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results. Although it newly attributes the baseline scores to Martin et al. (2025), the proposed method's results remain original contributions.

M1.justification: The operator interpolants, drift-learning objectives, posterior-sampling transformations, and Algorithms 1–2 are unchanged. The appendix retains the same model architectures and training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate MNIST, CelebA, AFHQ-Cat, phi4 fields, and maze trajectories with the same generation, inpainting, posterior-sampling, and planning tasks. Figure 8's replacement example does not expand coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains OT-ODE, D-Flow, Flow-Priors, and PnP-Flow. v4 identifies them through Pokle, Ben-Hamu, Zhang, and Martin citations; these are the same comparators already present in v1.

E3.justification: The stated protocols remain unchanged: 100 test images per image dataset, the same mask sizes and noise levels, PSNR/SSIM metrics, and Appendix B training settings. The phi4 and maze evaluation sample counts also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The posterior-magnetization comparison, field-inpainting demonstrations, and maze-validity checks are retained. No ablation, sensitivity study, robustness analysis, or focused case study is added or removed; Figure 8 refreshes illustrative outputs.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the benchmark results. The reporting of average reconstruction metrics and the magnetization histogram is unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 reverses the CelebA and AFHQ-Cat headers while retaining every numerical entry. Consequently, Ours' random-mask result 33.76/0.967 changes attribution from AFHQ-Cat to CelebA, while 33.11/0.945 changes in the opposite direction. This is a reported-result reassignment, not demonstrated performance improvement. Figure 8 also replaces one CelebA subject and its reconstructions.

T1.justification: The theoretical statements, assumptions, and proofs in Sections 2–3 and Appendices A–B are substantively unchanged. Restoring x arguments in equations (16)–(17) and removing a surplus parenthesis in (11) are notation corrections.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about operator-based interpolation, multitask generation without task-specific retraining, and competitive empirical performance.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the interpretations of inpainting quality, posterior sampling, and maze feasibility, including slight image over-smoothing. The training-complexity tradeoff and the applicability limitations discussed in Appendix B.2 are also unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 adds project-website and experiment-code links in the abstract footnotes. Section 5.1 newly states that all Table 1 rows except Ours come from Martin et al. (2025). Existing implementation, hyperparameter, and hardware disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds references for the four existing restoration baselines: Martin et al., Zhang et al., Ben-Hamu et al., and Pokle et al. Martin et al. also enters the inverse-problems related-work paragraph. The broader research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Changes comprise limited copyediting, notation cleanup, short baseline-attribution additions, an equal-contribution note, and a NeurIPS conference footer replacing the preprint notice. The section organization and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 is relocated and uses citation-based row labels. Figures 4 and 8 are rebuilt with revised labels, and Figure 8 reverses the dataset sides and mask-block order. Its caption still describes the old arrangement, creating a mismatch. Other figures are retained or relocated.

improvement.justification: v4 improves traceability through baseline citations, explicit score provenance, and code-access links. However, Table 1 reverses dataset assignments without explaining whether this corrects or introduces an error, and Figure 8's rearrangement introduces a caption mismatch. The PDFs establish these benefits and problems but do not support a reliable net-quality judgment.
